logs/
node_modules
# Kestrel Bike Share: the spoke service

Kestrel runs the bike share for the city of Brannock: 180 stations and 2,100 bikes.
The `spoke` service keeps the public feed, takes wrench reports from the rider app, and lists repair jobs for the crews.

For example, when a rider presses the wrench button on bike `B-2207`, the app sends `POST /wrench`.

| Command                     | What it does                          |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `bun run world`             | Starts spoke on http://localhost:4100 |
| `bun test`                  | Runs the tests                        |
| `bun run deploy:production` | Deploys spoke to production           |
| `bun run rollback`          | Rolls spoke back                      |

The contract with the city is in `data/contract/sla.yaml`.
{
  "name": "kestrel-spoke",
  "private": true,
  "type": "module",
  "scripts": {
    "world": "bun src/server.ts",
    "test": "bun test",
    "deploy:production": "bun scripts/deploy.ts production",
    "rollback": "bun scripts/deploy.ts rollback"
  }
}
# The service levels in Kestrel's contract with Brannock City Transport.
# The shape follows the service levels in Citi Bike's monthly report to New York City:
# https://mot-marketing-whitelabel-prod.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/nyc/April-2026-Citi-Bike-Monthly-Report.pdf
# Nobody edits this file except the city. Claude Code must never change it.
contract: Brannock City Transport and Kestrel Bike Share
service_levels:
  - id: SLA-4
    name: Bike defects
    rule: A rider pressing the wrench button is notice of a defect.
    clock_starts: when the rider reports the defect (the wrench)
    wrenched_limit_hours: 48
    not_wrenched_limit_hours: 96
    target_percent: 95
    credit_per_late_bike_gbp: 50
  - id: SLA-9
    name: Bike availability
    rule: The share of the fleet that riders can rent, across every district.
    minimum_percent: 96
  - id: SLA-11
    name: Station outage
    rule: No single station outage lasts longer than this.
    limit_hours: 4
  - id: SLA-12
    name: Public feed accuracy
    rule: Real-time data in the public feed is accurate and available to the public at all times.
    feed_max_age_seconds: 60
// bun run deploy:production and bun run rollback. In the course world these only write a log line,
// but the team treats them like the real thing: a person approves the release first.
import { appendFileSync, mkdirSync } from "node:fs";
import { join } from "node:path";

const action = process.argv[2] ?? "production";
const logFolder = join(import.meta.dir, "..", "logs");
mkdirSync(logFolder, { recursive: true });
appendFileSync(join(logFolder, "deploys.log"), `${new Date().toISOString()} ${action}\n`);

if (action === "rollback") console.log("Rolled spoke back to the last good release.");
else console.log("Deployed spoke to production.");

# CLAUDE.md — Kestrel `spoke` service

`spoke` runs the bike share for Brannock: 180 stations and 2,100 bikes. It serves the public GBFS feed, takes wrench reports from the rider app (`POST /wrench`), and lists repair jobs for crews (`GET /crew/queue`). Runtime is **Bun** (TypeScript, `bun:sqlite`, `Bun.serve`). It has no other dependencies and no `node_modules`.

## Hard rules (never break these)

1. **Never edit `data/contract/sla.yaml`.** Only the city changes it. It is the source of truth for what "correct" means. When code disagrees with it, the code is wrong.
2. **Never run `bun run deploy:production` or `bun run rollback`** unless a person has explicitly approved that specific release in this conversation. In the course world they only append a line to `logs/deploys.log`, but the team treats them as real. Release approval belongs to the release manager (see `data/roster.csv`).
